subject: Runway stitch & fallback playbook for AtlasAI (DL-4729)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Vega <carlos@atlasai.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Runway stitch & fallback playbook for AtlasAI (DL-4729)

Team —

Putting together a short weekly playbook to stitch AtlasAI's Q3 reserved commitment to our Dedicated fleet and a lightweight fallback if burst demand spikes. Atlas is close to signing DL-4729 and their close window is mid-July; they want predictable latency and a 24/7 support SLA for the first 90 days.

Attached: runway-matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) which maps forecasted token-hour demand to candidate GPU pools and fallback tiers. High level asks for this week:  
- Jordan: confirm which Dedicated pools can be pinned for a July start (rough node counts by family).
- Ben: rough burst credit estimate and ops lead for burst activation.
- Laura: pricing guidance if Atlas prefers a 12-month reserved commit vs 6-month ramp + burst.
- I'll own coordination with Atlas and the DocuSign flow once we lock terms.

Quick notes in the matrix: we conservatively assume 25% QoS buffer; fallback = region-based re-route + smaller quantized model (v2-q8) for non-critical traffic. If anyone needs a different fallback (e.g., multi-region warm standby), flag it now.

I'll run a 30-min sync Thursday to finalize numbers and the Action Item list for Sales/Infra/Finance.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Carlos Vega <carlos@atlasai.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runway stitch & fallback playbook for AtlasAI (DL-4729)

Stephanie —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the matrix. A couple of clarifications from our side:
1) The SLA window is critical for us during the pilot — we need <200ms median inference for the first 120M tokens/day.
2) Procurement prefers a 12-month commit if pricing is within 10% of your 6-month blended ramp. Procurement is copied on this thread (procurement@atlasai.com).

Can Jordan and Ben confirm the node fabric assumptions so we can finish our internal capacity planning?  Happy to join the sync Thursday.

— Carlos
Carlos Vega
Head of Product, AtlasAI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runway stitch & fallback playbook for AtlasAI (DL-4729)

Stephanie / Team —

Quick status on infra: we have two candidate Dedicated pools that match Atlas's latency/throughput profile — Pool-A (g5x2/64GB equivalence) and Pool-B (a100-lite). Summary:
- Pool-A: good for steady low-latency, estimated 12 nodes to cover the baseline (with 25% buffer).
- Pool-B: higher throughput for bursty jobs; we can provide 6 nodes as warm standby for the 30% burst envelope.

Notes / constraints:
- Pinning Pool-A for a July start requires order by 2027-06-14 to hit provisioning SLA.
- Warm standby on Pool-B can be architected as auto-burst: Ops will pre-warm 2 nodes and spin to 6 within 18 minutes; faster spin requires reserved capacity (extra cost).

Action for me: I'll export a nodal diagram and the provisioning ETA to the shared Box link before the Thursday sync.

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runway stitch & fallback playbook for AtlasAI (DL-4729)

Folks —

I've attached a short pricing sketch (commit-pricing.pdf) with two paths: 12-month reserved and 6-month ramp + burst credits. Highlights:
- 12-month: ~17% discount off on-demand across the pinned nodes; better predictability for Atlas and smoother revenue recognition for us.
- 6-month ramp + burst: lower upfront commitment; assumes Atlas pays higher burst unit rates and a 6-week runway to full commit.

Recommendation: push for 12-month if sales can meet the 10% gap Carlos mentioned. We can offer a mid-point blended price and a 90-day exit-trigger: if Atlas's 90-day SLA metrics are not met (latency or error rate), they'll get a break on month 3 billing — this reduces procurement friction.

Also: finance needs an explicit mapping of forecast token-hours to monthly invoice bands. Jordan — can you provide the Pool-A/B node counts as planned? Ben — we need burst unit assumptions (token-per-credit).

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Carlos Vega <carlos@atlasai.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runway stitch & fallback playbook for AtlasAI (DL-4729)

All —

Bursts and ops notes:
- Burst credit estimate: to cover a 30% demand spike over baseline for 2 weeks, Atlas would need ~1.2M burst credit units (estimate in runway-matrix_v1.xlsx).
- Ops lead: assigning Priya Natarajan (ops) as the on-call for the initial 90-day pilot (cc'ing her in the infra doc). She can coordinate warm standby / pre-warm windows with Jordan.
- Quick fallback plan: if region congestion occurs, we'll route up to 40% of non-critical traffic to the v2-q8 model (lower cost, slight quality delta). Critical traffic retains Pool-A.

Next steps (Thursday sync agenda):
1) Jordan: final node counts and provisioning ETA (Pool-A & Pool-B).
2) Laura: pricing sheet for 12-month mid-point blended offer + exit-trigger clause language.
3) Stephanie: run DocuSign flow and finalize the mutual action plan with Atlas.
4) Priya: draft ops play for warm standby activation (15 min runbook).
